---
title: "Marginal interval overlap and direction probabilities"
subtitle: "1.11 · two posterior intervals and one direction probability, after Kline, Rose and Walters (2024)"
description: "Pairwise direction probabilities associated with overlapping marginal credible intervals."
---

Consider independent normal posterior distributions for A and B with equal standard deviations. The upper figure
shows their central credible intervals; the lower figure shows the posterior distribution of the difference A − B.
The standard deviation of the difference is $\sqrt 2$ times the common posterior SD, whereas the sum of the two
marginal SDs is 2 times that quantity. Interval overlap and the probability of a positive difference consequently
measure different features of the posterior. A direction can have high posterior probability even when the marginal
intervals overlap substantially.

## Numerical illustrations {#what-to-try}

- **Just touch, 90%.** The intervals meet at 1.645, and the posterior means are 3.290 posterior SDs apart. The
  difference has SD 1.414, so they are 2.326 of its SDs apart, and A is very probably the higher: .990.
- **Just touch, 95%.** Wider intervals touch only farther apart, at 3.920 posterior SDs, so touching 95% intervals correspond to direction probability .997.
- **Means 2 SDs apart.** The intervals overlap by 1.290 posterior SDs, and the chance that A's true value is larger is
  still .921.
- **Means 1 SD apart.** An overlap of 2.290 posterior SDs corresponds to direction probability .760.

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}
When two 90% intervals just touch, A is very probably the higher, .990, for two independent normal posteriors with
equal SDs (.997 for 95% intervals). With unequal SDs the distance at which the intervals touch and the SD of the
difference change, and the probability with them. Kline, Rose and Walters (2024, section IV.C and Figure 3) draw a
credible interval beside each first name, but they grade the names from pairwise posterior probabilities, not from
whether the intervals overlap.
:::

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="In postrank"}
Sites D and E of the package's tutorial input have posterior means .15 and −.50 and SD .20 each, 3.250 posterior SDs
apart: the app at `?gap=3.25` gives the same probability, .989, with intervals that overlap by .040 posterior SDs.

```r
library(postrank); m <- postrank_posterior_means(pr_tutorial$one, level = .9)
attr(m, "upper")["E", 1] - attr(m, "lower")["D", 1]   # 0.007941451 = .040 × SD .20: the 90% intervals of D and E overlap
1 - pr_tutorial$one$e["D", "E", "score_A"]             # 0.9892219: the chance that D is truly higher
```
:::

Standalone: [embed/interval-overlap.html](../../embed/interval-overlap.html), for example `?gap=3.25` or
`?preset=touch95&theme=dark`.
